*Reproduce Steps:*

# Create a contract containing 2 PODs, each assigned to a different Billing Group.
# Add the required data and generate standard invoices. Verify that *2 invoices are generated* (one for each Billing Group).
# Create a new resigned contract using the same 2 PODs, assigning them again to the 2 Billing Groups. Ensure the selected Product has IAP enabled.
# Start the IAP generation run.

*Actual Result:*

Two interim invoices are generated with the same amount, based on the last generated invoice.

*Expected Result:*
The system should verify whether one POD is included in the corresponding invoice. If it is, the interim invoice should be generated based on that specific invoice associated with the POD, rather than reusing the amount from the last generated invoice.

GE Description:

When calculating an interim (% from previous invoice) for a billing group, if there is no invoice in the current billing and no invoice for the current contract for that billing group, the system must take the PODs of that billing group, find previous invoices for the same customer that include at least one of those PODs (from any contract where the POD was active), consider only invoices not older than three months, take the latest of those invoices, and use it as the basis for the interim amount for that billing group.

Hi, Valeri. Could you please specify exactly which part of the diagram should be working in your case? As I understand, when there are more than one invoices, we choose the latest, not one for each group.
I think the check for POD match is missing, so it takes the latest invoice

All of these billing groups belong to the same customer, but each invoice is associated with a different billing group. Therefore, the interim billing run cannot link these invoices by billing group because they are all different.
Additionally, interim invoices do not contain POD or detailed data, so they do not have a direct connection to a POD.

in this case we have 4 different customers , 2 used on volume invoices and another two used on interim invoices , so you mean interim billing run should take pods from billing group and check this pods used or not in another billing groups which has have generated real invoice ?

Valeri, please approve the logic we’ve covered on the meeting: When calculating an interim (% from previous invoice) for a billing group on a resigned contract, if there is no invoice in the current billing and no invoice for the current contract for that billing group, the system must take the PODs of that billing group on the new contract, find previous invoices (from any related billing group) that include at least one of those PODs and are not older than three months, take the latest of those invoices, and use it as the basis for the interim amount for that billing group.
We should not limit it only to resigned contract, but all contracts were the POD was active. Also should check if the customer is the same.
